title: Nimbus Commerce quick pitch notes
content:
Goal: quick notes to prep a short pilot ask to Nimbus Commerce (mid-market omnichannel retailer). Keep informal, jotty.

Background:
- Nimbus Commerce = mid-market retail tech (headless storefront + order orchestration). HQ SF, ~600 employees, Series B late 2023.
- Public-facing engineering hiring: backend (Go), platform (K8s), ML/AI team small (2 ICs) - likely using managed cloud infra (GCP).
- Product: merchant storefronts, search + recommendations, customer support portal. They launched a pilot of inline chat support last Q using vendor X (conversational bot) but reported latency / hallucination issues in merchant support threads.
- Why Redwood could fit: they care about predictable latency for chat/support flows, want private deployment options for merchant data, and cost control for wide-scale multi-tenant inference.

Notes to self / signals:
- Case studies: competitor vendor "Talkflow" used by Nimbus in 2025 for KB-based chat — reported 350–500ms avg response but high token cost on heavy traffic days (found in trade press interview).
- Security/regulatory: some enterprise merchants require data isolation — good door for Redwood Private.
- Risk: Nimbus has a small ML team, might not want heavy infra changes. Sell low-friction pilot + managed ops.

Outbound angle (short):
- Subject: Quick idea to cut chat latency and cost for Nimbus support
- 1-line open: Hey <Name>, noticed Nimbus flagged chat latency and hallucinations in your recent engineering blog — curious if a short pilot to reduce median response time and cut token spend would be interesting.
- CTA: 15–20 min intro + optional 2-week pilot using Redwood Hosted or Dedicated (we can scope).

Two-tier ask (prefer):
- 1) Quick benchmark: we run 500 synthetic support requests through Redwood-hosted equivalent models vs current setup — show latency/cost delta. (No infra changes for them; they share sample logs + non-sensitive prompts).
- 2) Pilot: 2-week Dedicated pool with canary routing (their test tenant), measure latency SLOs + cost per resolved conversation.

Draft cold message (short):
- Variant A (engineering lead):
  Hi <First>, Maya from Redwood Inference — saw Nimbus’ note about chat UX regression. We recently helped a headless storefront provider cut median chat latency from ~420ms to ~170ms and reduce per-conversation token spend by ~38% using targeted batching + prefix caching. Could we run a 15-min benchmark with 500 of your anonymized support prompts to show a head-to-head?

- Variant B (product/ops):
  Hi <First>, quick idea — we can run a no-code benchmark to surface latency and token-cost savings for Nimbus’ customer support chat. If numbers look good, a short Dedicated pilot is straightforward to stand up. 15 min to kick off?

Objection handling (cheat sheet):
- "We already have a vendor" -> acknowledge + offer win-win benchmark: "Totally — would you be open to a painless head-to-head on archival prompts? No infra changes, just results so you can compare objectively."
- "Security / PII concerns" -> mention Private deployment + KMS/HSM, audit logs, and option to run benchmark on client-side or with synthetic anonymized data; redact customer identifiers.
- "Cost / vendor lock" -> emphasize per-token transparency, model variants routing to cheaper quantized models for non-critical traffic, and predictable Dedicated pricing. Offer a cost-saver estimate based on sample logs.
- "We don’t have bandwidth" -> offer to run the benchmark with minimal engagement (we do import + transform) and deliver a one-pager results summary.

Pilot success metrics (what to measure):
- Median and 95th percentile latency for support chat responses (ms).
- Tokens per resolved conversation and cost delta (USD).
- Answer quality: top-1 acceptance rate by agent triage or automated BLEU/ROUGE-ish comparison on labeled set (use their evaluation prompts if available).
- Operational: number of incidents, error rate, and KB cache hit rate.

Technical checklist (for quick benchmark):
- Need: 500–1k anonymized prompt/response pairs (remove PII) OR synthetic prompts that mimic distribution.
- If they want on-prem/private: ask for network/ops contact + basic infra footprint (GPUs desired, VPC connectivity).
- For Hosted test: API keys + rate-limit baseline; we can sandbox via our hosted creds and return results CSV.

Call script highlights (10–15 min intro):
- 30s opener: credentials + one-paragraph result from similar customer.
- 2 min discovery: current stack for chat, main pain (latency/cost/quality), SLA targets.
- 3 min propose: quick benchmark + two-week pilot options, what we need.
- 2 min risk/objection: highlight data handling + rollback/fallback plan.
- 2 min next steps + scheduling pilot kickoff.

Experiment ideas (if they’re curious beyond chat):
- Embedded reranking for recommendation emails (cheap model for candidate scoring + Redwood rerank pipeline) — possible 15% CTR lift? (speculative).
- Prefix caching for repeat customer queries to reduce tokens on purchase flows.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Does Nimbus run inference in GCP only? Need confirmation (ask in first call).
- Who is the product lead for support chat? Looks like "Caroline Park" (LinkedIn) but need verification.
- Prep one-pager case study (similar customer) — ask Growth to share a redacted version. @Diego - can you pull the "headless storefront" case study draft?
- Build quick benchmark script in GH: gh repo TODO link (will attach).

Notes-to-self style reminders:
- Keep email short — they’re product-heavy, prefer data up front.
- Bring up Private option only after they confirm data isolation need; lead with hosted benchmark to lower friction.
- Price sensitivity likely: emphasize quantized model routing and opportunity to reduce costs quickly.

Revision history:
- 2026-02-25 initial brainstorm
- 2026-03-10 tuned messaging after scoping call with Priya (shortened pitch, added Hosted first approach)

End.
